objective: Replace aggregate-SSE cell routing with prompt-group distributionally robust support selection and prompt-normalized conditional scale fitting, while preserving v75's exact packed rate, bytes, codes, one-pass dispatch, and runtime operation count.

parent_finding.conclusion: Global scale shrinkage is already nearly optimal. The missing capacity is prompt-conditional correction direction, so select support under prompt-group risk rather than aggregate token SSE.

development_prompt_sets: four original disjoint v42 validation prompts

estimator.fixed_int4_codes: v75 signed INT4 source-weight codes in [-8, 7], group 128, from four deterministic weight-space scale iterations
estimator.fit_environments: eight calibration prompts with deterministic row ownership
estimator.environment_loss: per-prompt per-output-tile SSE divided by that prompt tile's initial CQ3 residual SSE
estimator.conditional_scale_fit: shared nonnegative row scale minimizing the equally weighted normalized prompt-environment loss, rounded to FP16 before scoring
estimator.robust_marginal_score: mean normalized marginal SSE reduction across prompts minus one population standard deviation
estimator.selection: at each step and output tile choose the unselected input cell with maximum robust marginal score, then update every prompt residual exactly

data_status.reason: The estimator family was selected after v74-v77 diagnostics.
data_status.allowed_use: Reject or admit the fixed estimator to a second newly authored prompt replication only.

decision.if_pass: Freeze the exact support, codes, and scales, then create a second untouched non-benchmark prompt cache for replication before representative-layer work.
decision.if_fail: Reject mean-minus-standard-deviation prompt-robust routing without relaxing this gate or sweeping risk radius on either development set.

claim_boundary: Development-only layer-59 screen of a frozen prompt-group robust support estimator. Even a pass can only authorize a second new-prompt replication; it cannot establish whole-model quality, benchmark retention, CPU speed, energy, novelty, 100 tokens per second, or a breakthrough.
